claims.text: Laser surface alloying can uniformly incorporate approximately 0.5 atomic percent yttrium into an as-sprayed NiCoCrFeAl bond coat while minimizing thermal stresses and microstructural damage.
Laser-alloyed yttrium will segregate to grain boundaries during high-temperature cycling.
Yttrium segregation will facilitate the nucleation and uniform growth of a protective alumina scale.
The treatment will rapidly form a continuous alumina scale.
The alumina scale produced by the treatment will be adherent.
A continuous and adherent alumina scale will form along grain boundaries and at the bond-coat surface.
Yttrium incorporation will reduce oxide-scale discontinuities.
Yttrium incorporation will reduce thermal-mechanical mismatch.
The laser-alloyed coating will have better oxidation resistance than an untreated as-sprayed NiCoCrFeAl bond coat.
The laser-alloyed coating will exhibit less oxide spallation than the untreated baseline.
The laser-alloyed coating will develop fewer crack-initiation sites than the untreated baseline.
The treatment will improve bonding integrity between the bond coat and the overlying thermal-barrier coating.
The proposed benefits will remain effective during cyclic oxidation and rapid thermal cycling at approximately 1100 degrees Celsius.
Nonuniform yttrium distribution may limit the effectiveness of the intervention.
Microstructural coarsening during prolonged high-temperature exposure may limit the effectiveness of the intervention.
